summary: Add the independently audited max common-terminal A_mu boundary theorem: an exact moving-event response formula, uniform all-q positivity for sufficiently small positive contrast at each fixed n, and the positive q-to-infinity limit at each fixed finite contrast. The remaining finite interior and general max/O3a stay open; no existing node is changed.

node.title: Wronskian response and event-pair compactification orient the max A_mu boundary regimes
node.statement: The accepted finite full-relay structure and reflection-fixed max common-terminal order imply the exact fixed-q A_mu response formula and the two boundary-regime positivity conclusions stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MAX-AMU-BOUNDARY-R24.

node.title: Positive max common-terminal A_mu at the small-contrast and large-q boundaries
node.statement: Fix finite R>1, integer n>=2, and a premise-complete transverse max-law common-terminal root A_n(mu,q)=0 with mu>1 and q>1. With Delta_i=rho(t_i+)-rho(t_i-), J_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu)U_i^2, and I_V=integral rho V^2, one has the exact fixed-q identity partial_mu A_n=[2mu I_V-(q^2-1)J_mu]/q^2 and its equivalent Pohozaev form from the proof package. For every fixed n there exists epsilon_n>0 such that every such root with 1<R<1+epsilon_n has partial_mu A_n>0 uniformly over all q>1. For each fixed finite R>1, every sequence of such roots with q tending to infinity satisfies mu tending to (n+1)/n, L tending to n pi, and partial_mu A_n tending to n^2 pi/(n+1)>0. No positivity is asserted on the remaining finite-contrast bounded-q interior, in a simultaneous R,q to infinity scaling, or at relay-chart degeneracies.

node.title: Orient max A_mu on the remaining finite interior
node.statement: Prove the fixed-q common-terminal orientation partial_mu A_n>0 for every remaining finite-contrast max root, or provide an exact or certified full physical counterexample; R24 already excludes fixed-n small positive contrast and the fixed-finite-R q-to-infinity end.
node.formal_statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and every premise-complete transverse max-law common-terminal root, prove J_mu<2mu I_V/(q^2-1), equivalently partial_mu A_n>0. It remains to control the bounded-q finite-contrast interior, q approaching 1, high-contrast/noncompact limits, and simultaneous R,q divergence, while retaining all moving-event saltation and endpoint terms; alternatively certify a complete physical root with partial_mu A_n<=0.
discharge_criteria: Cover every finite R>1 and n>=2 strict max common-terminal root outside the two R24 boundary regimes, including both midpoint parities and all compatible relay chambers.
Retain rho_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu)delta_(t_i); omitting the moving-event term invalidates the orientation problem.
Treat q approaching 1, R approaching infinity, simultaneous large R and q, grazing, collision, incomplete words, and nontransverse limits separately.
Do not infer partial_mu A_n>0 from partial_q A_n>0 or fixed-mu cell order without a noncircular fixed-q frequency or equivalent global response estimate.
Any counterexample must satisfy the full physical relay, common-terminal, event-count, and transversality predicates; scalar ledgers and local-cell witnesses do not discharge this obligation.

node.title: Max common-terminal A_mu Wronskian and compactified boundary route
node.statement: Use exact parameter Wronskians, Pohozaev identities, a uniform R=1 labelled word, and a blown-up q-to-infinity event-pair analysis to orient partial_mu A_n at both boundary regimes. The finite-contrast bounded-q interior, norm orientation, full residual Jacobian, uniqueness, and general O3a remain open.
node.method_family: Moving-event Wronskians, Pohozaev identities, Chebyshev event counting, uniform transfer bounds, blown-up paired-event implicit-function analysis, and one-point compactification of q
node.deliverable_contract: An exact all-root A_mu reduction and rigorous positivity on the fixed-n small-positive-contrast and fixed-finite-R large-q boundary regimes, without extending the result to the unresolved finite interior.
falsification_tests: Check the right-minus-left jump convention and the minus sign in rho_mu=-sum Delta_i t_(i,mu)delta_(t_i).
At R=1 prove exactly 2n simple labelled events for every finite q>=1; do not assume the word persists at q=1 without a double-root audit.
In the q-to-infinity limit prove paired event-velocity cancellation O(1/q), not merely boundedness of individual event velocities.
Keep the collapse estimates uniform only on bounded finite-contrast ranges and do not compactify a simultaneous R,q-to-infinity limit.
Do not use numerical scans, the implication-level wrong-sign scalar ledger, or the blocked phase-field subtraction as theorem premises.
node.expected_bottleneck: The exact event response J_mu is unsigned on the remaining finite-contrast bounded-q interior; accepted fixed-mu q-twist information controls J_q instead and does not orient J_mu.

ordered_steps: At a reflection-fixed max common-terminal root differentiate both scalar zero times at fixed q, including rho_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu)delta_(t_i). The event identity U_i^2=mu^2V_i^2 and p^2=1, r^2=q^2 give partial_mu A_n=[2mu I_V-(q^2-1)J_mu]/q^2 with J_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu)U_i^2.

Apply the two piecewise Pohozaev identities to obtain the equivalent dilation-remainder formula; this confirms every jump and endpoint sign without replacing J_mu by the independently signed q-response.

At R=1 show L_0=n pi, mu_0=(n+1)/n and partial_mu A_n=L_0/mu_0>0 for every finite q>=1. Chebyshev factorization, nodal interlacing, and the double-root identity prove that the labelled word has exactly 2n simple events even at the q=1 closure.

For fixed n and bounded finite contrast, normalize Z=V/q and eta=1/q. Uniform transfer bounds and the forced nodal allocation confine each positive material cell to an O(eta) neighborhood of a simple high-mode zero. Blow up all event pairs and apply the finite-dimensional C1 implicit-function theorem; the limiting event Jacobian is diagonal and nonzero, so paired mu-velocity differences are O(eta), J_mu=O(eta), and I_V/q^2=L_0/(2mu_0^2)+O(eta).
Substitute these estimates into the exact response formula to obtain mu to mu_0, L to L_0, and partial_mu A_n to n^2 pi/(n+1)>0 for q tending to infinity at each fixed finite R.

If no uniform small-positive-contrast epsilon_n existed, take R_k to 1 with nonpositive partial_mu A_n. Sturm comparison forces mu_k to mu_0 and L_k to L_0. A bounded-q subsequence converges through the simple R=1 labelled word, while an unbounded-q subsequence is covered by the uniform pair-collapse lemma; both give the same positive limit, a contradiction.
boundary_cases: The theorem includes n=2 and every fixed n>=2 but the small-contrast constant may depend on n.
Both terminal parities are covered because only p^2 and r^2 enter the response formula; R9 supplies reflection fixing for every max common-terminal root.
The q=1 point and R=1 word are used only as proved one-sided labelled closures; the theorem concerns strict q>1 and R>1 roots.
The q-to-infinity estimates are uniform only on bounded finite-contrast ranges. No claim is made for simultaneous R,q divergence or R tending to infinity.
Grazing, collision, zero event amplitude, incomplete words, and nontransverse roots are outside the strict chart and are not differentiated by assertion.
The remaining finite-contrast bounded-q interior, universal A_mu sign, norm slope, full residual Jacobian, uniqueness, and max O3a remain open.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: R24 proves the exact response and excludes two boundary regimes, but J_mu remains unsigned on the finite-contrast bounded-q interior and in noncompact high-contrast scalings. This intermediate orientation is also insufficient by itself to prove the norm slope or general max/O3a.

The route rigorously closes the fixed-n small-positive-contrast and fixed-finite-R large-q regimes, while the universal finite-interior A_mu orientation and all downstream norm/Jacobian/uniqueness claims remain open.
